findings.title: Reject non-object JSON in required completion evidence
findings.trigger: A required .status.json, .boundary.json, .grader-provenance.json, or .base-status.json contains valid non-object JSON such as null or [].
findings.execution_path: completion_gate._read parses the JSON, returns None without appending a reason, and the caller skips validation under its `if ... is not None` guard. _completion_gate_main consequently returns exit 0 when the remaining checks pass.
findings.consequence: The operator's COMPLETE gate can pass without a complete report, verified boundary, established grader provenance, or required cross-grade.
findings.evidence: With a matching inspection-only meta record requiring cross-grading and all four required evidence records supplied as `null`, the actual gate printed `{"gate":"pass",...,"reasons":[]}` and returned 0. Existing gate tests exercise missing files and invalid object fields but omit valid JSON of the wrong top-level type.
findings.suggested_fix: Append an explicit invalid-record reason whenever parsed JSON is not an object. Add parameterized tests for null, arrays, strings, numbers, and booleans in every required record, asserting CLI exit 3.
findings.reproduction_command: python3 -B -c 'import json; from pathlib import Path; from unittest.mock import patch; from tests import codex_review_run as r; meta={"head":"a"*40,"base":"b"*40,"attempt":1,"review_mode":"inspection-only-ci-evidence","audited_inputs_changed_in_diff":["tests/codex_report_status.py"]}; read=lambda directory,name,**kw: json.dumps(meta).encode() if name.endswith(".meta.json") else b"null"; p=patch.object(r,"safe_read_regular_file",side_effect=read); p.start(); print(r._completion_gate_main(Path(".planning/phases/x/codex/aaaaaaaaaaaa-review-a1"))); p.stop()'

findings.title: Audit tool types on item-start and item-update events
findings.trigger: The event stream records a disallowed tool in item.started or item.updated without a corresponding item.completed event.
findings.execution_path: audit_event_types allows both top-level event types but examines their item types only for item.completed. _execute_inspection proceeds to grading when the returned reasons list is empty.
findings.consequence: The mandatory audit does not reject recorded tool activity unless its completion event is also present. If the report and process exit otherwise pass grading, this stream can be treated as an inspection-only review.
findings.evidence: Supplying an item.started event containing command_execution followed by turn.completed returned []. All disallowed-item regression fixtures use item.completed, including the orchestration test, so they do not cover this gap. This reproduces the audit defect, not live tool execution.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate item.type for every item-bearing event, including started and updated. Add start-only and update-only tool fixtures and an orchestration assertion that grading is never reached for either.
findings.reproduction_command: python3 -B -c 'import json; from pathlib import Path; from unittest.mock import patch; from tests import codex_review_run as r; stream="\n".join(json.dumps(e) for e in [{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"tool1","type":"command_execution","command":"id"}},{"type":"turn.completed"}]); p=patch.object(Path,"exists",return_value=True); q=patch.object(Path,"read_text",return_value=stream); p.start(); q.start(); print(r.audit_event_types(Path("mock.jsonl"))); q.stop(); p.stop()'
